R141.note: Adds @csrf_protect matching the existing secure sibling route; clean.

R142.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes replaces seeded Random correctly; now-unused seed param openly flagged.

R143.note: Policy-based authorize() check on ownership added correctly; owner still succeeds.

R144.note: Strict alnum/dot/hyphen allowlist fully blocks shell metacharacters; keeps cmd /C shell (not ideal shape) but vector is closed.

R145.note: Allowlist mapping to canonical module names closes dynamic import injection cleanly.

R146.note: jwt.verify() with algorithm allowlist replaces unsigned decode; try/catch preserves error handling.

R148.note: Removes IgnoreAntiforgeryToken and restores ValidateAntiForgeryToken; correct.

R149.note: Same correct PreparedStatement pattern as sibling case.

R150.note: Rejects absolute paths and verifies normalized containment against root; solid defense-in-depth.

R151.note: OWASP Encoder Encode.forHtml() at the exact sink; preserves rendering of normal names.

R152.note: Adds SigningMethodRSA type check in keyfunc, the standard golang-jwt algorithm-confusion fix.

R153.note: DTO separation of IsAdmin from client input is the right defense, but switching the wire format gob->json without showing/confirming the producer side also changes is undisclosed and could break every legitimate decode; only the signature change is disclosed.

R154.note: Rejects absolute paths and verifies toRealPath() containment; correct layered fix.

R155.note: AST-allowlist evaluator correctly blocks calls/attribute access while preserving arithmetic formulas.

R156.note: text() with named bind parameter, textbook SQLAlchemy Core fix.

R157.note: strnlen(name, sizeof(name)) correctly bounds the read.

R158.note: snprintf replaces strcpy/strcat; rejection of oversized input on truncation is explicitly disclosed.

R159.note: json_decode replacing unserialize() closes the gadget-chain vector, but switches wire format from PHP's native serialize (implied by the existing base64+unserialize pairing) without any compatibility note - existing cart cookies would likely decode to empty silently; unserialize($payload,['allowed_classes'=>false]) would have closed it while staying format-compatible.

R160.note: Tika magic-byte detection replaces trusted Content-Type header; re-encoding, size cap and CREATE_NEW are all explicitly disclosed additions.

R161.note: Bounds check switched to segment.size() (the authoritative bound) instead of the untrusted claimedCapacity; minimal and correct.

R162.note: Parameterized DB::select with '?' binding, standard Laravel fix.

R163.note: createElement/textContent/appendChild replaces innerHTML; preserves the same visual layout.

R164.note: new JexlSandbox() defaults to allow=true (verified in Apache Commons JEXL source: no-arg ctor is `this(true, false, null)`), so unlisted classes remain fully accessible - the .allow() calls are redundant and the sandbox does not actually restrict anything; vulnerability remains open. Needs new JexlSandbox(false).

R165.note: secrets.randbelow(max-min+1)+min correctly reproduces random.randint's inclusive range with a CSPRNG.

R166.note: Length check against frameBuffer.size() before memcpy correctly prevents the OOB read; rejects only invalid frames.

R167.note: Removes the no-op SignatureValidator, restoring the framework's real signature/issuer/audience checks.

R168.note: Rejects absolute paths and '..' then verifies Clean()'d path is prefix-contained in base; solid, minor edge case of legitimate filenames containing '..' substrings is a trivial false positive.

R169.note: Argument list with default shell=False removes shell interpretation entirely; command structure unchanged.

R170.note: SecureRandom.nextFloat() is a drop-in replacement for Random.nextFloat(); same downstream cookie logic.

R171.note: sanitizer.sanitize(SecurityContext.HTML, rawBody) before bypassSecurityTrustHtml correctly closes the raw-input bypass; DOMPurify offered as alternative.

R172.note: Same correct PreparedStatement pattern applied through the 4-file call chain.

R173.note: count > Integer.MAX_VALUE/size divides by size, which the existing validation allows to be 0 - a legitimate size=0 request (previously producing a valid 0-length buffer) now throws an unhandled ArithmeticException, undisclosed.

R174.note: htmlspecialchars at the exact reported sink; extra escaping of ticketId is explicitly called out as added defense-in-depth.

R175.note: Structured logging template/argument form is the standard .NET CWE-117 mitigation, replacing string interpolation.

R176.note: Replaces Runtime.exec() entirely with Files.newDirectoryStream; added absolute/traversal path rejection is disclosed as intentional hardening.

R177.note: offset + length > capacity correctly rejects the documented case, but offset and length are unsigned size_t so a large enough offset makes the sum wrap around and bypass the check (classic integer-overflow-in-bounds-check gap); no observable change for normal inputs though.

R178.note: The AST validator only inspects 'using' directives and exact-substring method names; a fully-qualified call like System.IO.File.Delete(...) needs no using directive and isn't in the ForbiddenMethods list, so the dangerous-API bypass this fix is meant to close largely remains for a determined attacker.

R179.note: Inserts '--' end-of-options marker before filenames, the correct fix for argv-based option/flag injection that a bare argument array alone doesn't close.

R180.note: fileTypeFromBuffer(file.buffer) runs inside multer's fileFilter, but multer's own source shows the file object passed to fileFilter has no buffer/stream property yet (those are attached only after fileFilter accepts the file) - file.buffer is always undefined there, so every upload throws and is rejected via the catch block; the endpoint is completely broken for all legitimate uploads, undisclosed.
